editorial.headline: A KBLI for Milling Root, Rhizome, and Vegetable Flours
editorial.standfirst: Code 10613 covers the industrial making of flour from tubers, rhizome plants, and vegetables, open across business scales and not marked as Bali-blocked in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10613 is a manufacturing classification for turning varied tubers, rhizome plants, and vegetables into flour through milling. The Indonesian scope names the activity plainly: making flour from cassava gaplek, sweet potato, taro, irut, ginger, temulawak, turmeric, cardamom, and vegetables. Its centre of gravity is not retail, farming, or food service; it is the processing step where plant material is milled into a flour product.

That makes the code useful for founders who need a clear industrial home for a flour-making operation built around these agricultural inputs. The record opens the activity to every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. In practical classification terms, that breadth matters because the code is not reserved only for large factories or only for small local producers. The same activity description can accommodate a modest milling operation and a larger industrial setup, provided the actual business remains within the recorded scope.

The national foreign-investment picture is straightforward. The record marks PMA status as TERBUKA and gives the maximum foreign ownership as 100%. That is the only ownership percentage in the record, and it is national. There is no separate Bali percentage, quota, partnership condition, capital threshold, or special local formula stated here. The cited PMA source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, and the editorial conclusion must stay inside that boundary: nationally, this activity is open to foreign ownership up to the recorded ceiling.

Bali is also not marked as blocked for this code in the slim record. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with the reason stated as: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium text still matters as context because it says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide and permanently. But for this record, the stated Bali-side conclusion is that the activity is not blocked by that moratorium. The honest reading is therefore clean: KBLI 10613 is nationally open to PMA up to 100%, and the Bali fields do not mark it as blocked today.
